strings: You carry an arcane communion gem to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity, after winning Gunther Arcanus's trust and restoring his grimoire.

Gunther Arcanus spent years alone on an island in Brightwater Lake. By sheer force of will, he broke free from the Lich King's control, unaware that Sylvanas Windrunner had liberated Lordaeron. Bitter and wary of outsiders, he distrusted the Undercity's emissaries. An adventurer returned his spellbook and showed him their hostility toward the Scourge. Satisfied the visitor was no enemy, Gunther entrusted them with a Nether Gem to contact his former colleague.

You return to the Undercity's Magic Quarter and deliver the Nether Gem to Bethor Iceshard. Bethor channels its power and conjures Gunther's ethereal visage in the sanctuary. Through their magical communion, Gunther formally agrees to ally with the Forsaken cause. Gaining a necromancer of his independent mastery bolsters the Dark Lady's young kingdom and its magical defenses against the Scourge and the living.

Gunther Arcanus is a powerful necromancer who broke free of the Lich King's mental domination by himself. He lived in reclusive exile on an island in Brightwater Lake, believing all other undead were mindless thralls until adventurers proved otherwise.
gunther arcanus lore | who is the prodigal lich | gunther undercity
Bethor Iceshard is a senior mage and scholar who lives in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. An old colleague of Gunther Arcanus, he coordinated the effort to find and recruit him into the Forsaken.
bethor lore | who is bethor | iceshard undercity
What does the Nether Gem do?

Gunther Arcanus gave Bethor Iceshard the Nether Gem, an enchanted artifact. When Bethor channels arcane power into it, the gem manifests a spectral image of Gunther so the spellcasters can speak across great distances.
what is the nether gem | gunther gem
Why does Gunther agree to join the Forsaken?

Gunther spent years fearing he was Lordaeron's only free-willed undead. Convinced that Sylvanas's Forsaken are free of the Scourge and fight the Lich King, he willingly pledges allegiance and renews ties with his former peers.
Why does the quest call Gunther a 'Lich'?

Gunther looks like any Forsaken, rather than a floating, frost-wreathed Scourge lich, yet the Forsaken call him one. A Kirin Tor student and skilled necromancer in life, he was raised by the plague during the Third War and later broke the Lich King's hold by himself.

When you deliver the Nether Gem, Bethor activates it and conjures Gunther's Visage in the Magic Quarter. The projection moves toward Bethor to begin their long-awaited reunion, then fades.

Bethor's communion with Gunther joins traditional Dalaran spellcraft with the dark necromancy practiced in the Undercity's Magic Quarter.
Recruiting an independent master necromancer like Gunther strengthens the Horde's magical standing in the Eastern Kingdoms.
Gunther's freedom without the Banshee Queen's help shows the willpower Lordaeron's fallen can muster.
Why does Gunther Arcanus need you to deliver the Nether Gem?

Gunther Arcanus remains isolated on his island in Brightwater Lake, maintaining his cautious seclusion while he re-establishes contact with the world beyond. As an emissary who proved your loyalty by recovering his spellbook and destroying his necromantic enemies, you have earned his trust. Handing you the Nether Gem allows him to reach out to his old comrade Bethor Iceshard and negotiate his allegiance without having to abandon his sanctuary or march straight into the Undercity.

In Kharanos, Razzle Sprysprocket and Ozzie Togglevolt seek a cure for their kin. After Gnomeregan's fall, they hope an experimental machine can reverse the change that made many gnomes leper gnomes.

Radiation meant to purge the troggs in Gnomeregan changed most of the city's gnomes into sickly, deranged leper gnomes instead. Razzle Sprysprocket refuses to accept that this change must last. Working with Ozzie Togglevolt, the inventor is building a machine called the Recombobulator to restore their afflicted kin to health and sanity.

Razzle needs Restabilization Cogs and Gyromechanic Gears to build a delicate prototype. The parts come from the hostile leper gnomes outside Gnomeregan's sealed gates. Razzle hopes the debris taken from their altered kin will help build a device to undo the tragedy they share.
What is the Recombobulator supposed to do?
Razzle Sprysprocket and Ozzie Togglevolt designed the Recombobulator to reverse the effects of Gnomeregan's radiation and cure leper gnomes.

Razzle Sprysprocket and Ozzie Togglevolt are gnomish inventors working in Kharanos, in Dun Morogh. Since Gnomeregan fell, they have devoted their skills to finding ways to save their displaced, irradiated people.

As an engineer, you can appreciate Razzle's unorthodox work with Restabilization Cogs, crank-o-ratchets, and viscous electrogum gel to manipulate biophysical radiation.
For gnomes, this work offers a desperate hope of saving family and friends, changed into violent shells during the fall of their capital.
Why does Razzle Sprysprocket want this done?

The fall of Gnomeregan did not just leave the city overrun by troggs; the radiation released during the catastrophe twisted the vast majority of the gnomish population into mindless, hostile leper gnomes. Razzle Sprysprocket and his partner Ozzie refuse to accept that their people are lost forever. They believe their invention, the Recombobulator, can reverse the terrible afflictions of the fallout and restore the gnomish race to its former self.

What are the Restabilization Cogs and Gyromechanic Gears for?

These precision components are essential mechanical parts needed to finish building the Recombobulation Device according to Ozzie's intricate schematics. Once assembled into the apparatus alongside hydrolubricant, crank-o-ratchets, and electrogum gel, the gears and cogs will balance and regulate the machinery designed to undo the radiation that corrupted the leper gnomes.

Who are you sent against at Gnomeregan?

You are dispatched to hunt down the leper gnomes prowling outside the entrance gates of Gnomeregan. Formerly ordinary citizens, their minds and bodies were warped by the toxic radiation deployed to purge the trogg invasion. Driven mad, they now carry the scavenged machinery, gears, and cogs from the ruined city while violently attacking anyone who approaches.

Talo Thornhoof, a hunter at Camp Mojache in Feralas, believes knowing an enemy well can turn a battle. Talo sends you to Felwood, north of Ashenvale, to face the fel-tainted bears and wolves and learn whether they have truly grown stronger.

Talo Thornhoof is a hunter who strives to copy the strengths seen in opponents, and believes simply knowing an enemy well can turn a battle your way. Felwood lies north of Ashenvale, where a substance called fel has tainted the creatures. Talo thinks the bears and wolves there, driven mad by it, have also grown even stronger. Angerclaw grizzlies and Felpaw ravagers are the ones to face, twelve of each. Fel-touched things give off a strange green glow, which Talo senses is evil yet very powerful.
After your account of the beasts, Talo concludes they show a mindless ferocity, and warns you to stay alert and learn more of the corruption, since an enemy should always be known.

Latronicus Moonspear in Feathermoon Stronghold says a courier and the parcels he carried went missing about a week ago. The stronghold's own searches found nothing, so the courier is declared missing in action, and you are sent to Ginro Hearthkindle, who is seeking help.

Latronicus Moonspear has reached an impasse. A courier has been missing for about a week along with the parcels he was carrying, and the stronghold's own searches have been fruitless, so Latronicus has declared him missing in action. An associate, Ginro Hearthkindle, is looking for help with the matter and should be in Feathermoon Stronghold, perhaps in his quarters. Latronicus asks that you speak with Ginro, if you have time and means to spare.

Ginro knows that Latronicus, whom Ginro calls Latro, sent you. Ginro thinks it a lost cause, yet takes whatever help is offered, and longs to put the matter to rest. Each day Ginro heads out into Feralas to look for signs of Raschal, and each night comes back with only gnoll teeth and disappointment.
A courier who vanished about a week ago along with the parcels he carried. The stronghold's searches found nothing, and he has been declared missing in action.

Ginro Hearthkindle tells you the courier, Raschal, set out for Thalanaar about a week ago, planning to row down the coast. Ginro could not find the boat and asks you to look for it along the coast of Feralas, in case it holds a clue to where Raschal is.

About a week ago Raschal set out for Thalanaar. Raschal knows Feralas well and has been with the expeditionary forces since General Feathermoon led them here. Ginro's understanding is that Raschal meant to go by row boat down the coast and cross southern Feralas, avoiding the Horde camp. Ginro could not find the boat, which may be hidden or sunk, and asks you to look for it along the coast of Feralas, since it might hold a clue to where Raschal is. On the mainland, the Forgotten Coast stretches south from the jetty.

Through slightly muddy water you spot a wrecked row boat, riddled with gaping holes along one side and shredded nearly down to its wooden frame. Whatever broke it probably tried to split it in half. A small crest of Feathermoon Stronghold is painted on the other side, and in the mud at the boat's base something metallic glints.

Beside a wrecked row boat in the water you find a well-cared-for knife in the mud. Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold wants any clue you find brought back, and a feeling creeps over you that something else shares the water.

Feeling along the mud near the wrecked boat, your fingertips brush the grip of a knife that looks well cared for. Whoever was on the boat may have lost it, and the large chunk missing from the boat might have a part in the loss. You take the knife, recalling that Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold asked you to bring any clue you found back to him, yet the feeling creeps over you that something else shares the water.

Ginro believes the knife is Raschal's and asks whether you really found it on the bottom with his boat. The knife alone may not be enough to connect the boat to Raschal's disappearance, but there is an unconventional option for learning more, and Ginro asks whether you have ever heard of psychometry.

Ginro Hearthkindle sends you with the knife to Quintis Jonespyre, the Stronghold's resident druid, who can learn an object's past by touching it. Ginro says Quintis owes a Kalimdor Hold 'Em debt that this will clear.

After Boat Wreckage, Ginro Hearthkindle sends you with the knife to Quintis Jonespyre, the resident druid of Feathermoon Stronghold, who has unusual skills. One is psychometry, learning an object's past just by touching it. Ginro will not say how it works, calling it magic Ginro does not and chooses not to understand, only that Ginro has seen it work. Quintis owes Ginro a Kalimdor Hold 'Em debt, which will be paid if Quintis works some magic on the knife. Quintis lives in a little tree-house in the Stronghold.

Quintis says the psychometric readings drain the psyche, much as the losses at Kalimdor Hold 'Em do, and the Stronghold calls Quintis the King of the Bad Beats: unlucky at cards, lucky at the secrets of nature. Quintis agrees to do it, hoping the knife brings the breakthrough needed to uncover Raschal's fate.

Quintis thanks you, noting that psychometry is no exact art, but he has used it before to shed light on situations that others wrote off as lost causes. He expects the knife to give a glimpse of what happened to Raschal. It takes only a moment, though it is hard going for a caster, and Quintis asks you to bear with it.

At Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew sends a fresh barrel of Shimmer Stout to his brother Wellart. Wellart guards the pass toward Loch Modan, where a cold post makes a strong drink welcome.
A Family Recipe on the Frontier

Rejold Barleybrew has perfected Shimmer Stout with shimmering fronds gathered from Dun Morogh’s icy crags. His family tends the vats and kegs of Brewnall Village, but his brother Wellart chose life as a Mountaineer. Rejold knows how lonely frontier guard duty can be, so he sends a fresh barrel with passing travelers. It is a favor between brothers and a chance to test the brew.

Wellart Barleybrew guards the South Gate Pass into Loch Modan from the southern tower. High in the pass, Mountaineers face bitter winds and occasional beast attacks while watching over travelers on the mountain road. Wellart is running low on drink and restless for excitement. Shimmer Stout packs quite a punch, he finds, and seems to brighten his vision in the dim mountain night.

Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew is Rejold Barleybrew’s brother. While his kin brew ale in Brewnall Village, Wellart serves with the Dun Morogh Mountaineers, watching the high pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan.

As an Alliance traveler, you help keep the Mountaineers supplied as they guard the highway between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan.
As a dwarf, you know sharing ale with family matters as much as guarding the mountain passes. This delivery is part of frontier life in Ironforge.
Why does Rejold Barleybrew want this done?

Rejold is eager to share the fruits of his craft with his brother, Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew. Having just perfected his new recipe for Shimmer Stout at the family distillery, Rejold knows that while Wellart walked away from the brewing trade to patrol the borders, he remains a true dwarf at heart who loves a hearty drink. Delivering a fresh barrel is both a gesture of brotherly pride and a way to get an honest verdict on his latest concoction from a thirsty soldier in the field.

Quintis Jonespyre, still wobbly after reading the knife, passes on visions of Raschal and the Woodpaw gnolls and asks you to take them to Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold.

Quintis Jonespyre is still unsteady but has seen something useful. In the vision Raschal pulls two big leather backpacks off the boat, heads inland, and then goes back to the boat. Gnoll scalps appear, and Quintis thinks Raschal met Woodpaw gnolls. Raschal is very worried, almost terrified, and does not notice water elementals forming behind. There the images stop. Quintis must rest and asks you to tell Ginro, who needs to know.

Ginro thanks you for carrying Quintis's visions. Raschal can handle a fight, and gnolls would not worry Raschal, let alone terrify. Even so, Ginro hopes you and your companions can act on this and make the breakthrough that is badly needed.

After Quintis's vision, Ginro Hearthkindle sends you to search the camps of the Woodpaw gnolls in southern Feralas for evidence of the courier or the courier's belongings. Ginro doubts the gnolls were Raschal's undoing, but they are the best place to start.

Ginro Hearthkindle allows that the Woodpaw, whom Ginro puts in quotation marks as friends, may have done for Raschal in the end, though something tells Ginro otherwise. Still, they are the best place to start. Ginro has no clearer plan than searching their camps, and knows gnolls keep what they scavenge and fight over it, so they may have come across the backpacks Quintis mentioned. In past searches Ginro steered clear of open fighting, but with the vision to go on now says to rip into them. The camps lie in southern Feralas.
Two large leather backpacks are tacked to a nearby tree, and each carries a small insignia of Feathermoon Stronghold on its front. They are in the Lower Wilds.

Among the backpacks lies a hurried note signed by Raschal of Feathermoon. He writes of bug-like creatures he came across, and of his decision to look into them himself. Your search for him now leads there.

The backpacks hold a parcel meant for Thalanaar, and a note scribbled in a hurry to no one in particular. Its author, Raschal of Feathermoon, describes insidious bug-like creatures he discovered in the Writhing Deep, south of the gnoll camps. He felt he had to see them with his own eyes, for they seemed a grave danger to all of Feralas. The note shows where he went.

In the Writhing Deep you come upon a large pod of an alien kind. Its surface looks mucous, with hardened growths jutting from it here and there. It is tall and broad enough to hold a person, and through its skin you can make out the faint shape of a humanoid, which you take to be what it holds.

A cask of Rejold Barleybrew’s new Shimmer Stout is bound for Mountaineer Kadrell in Loch Modan. You carry the brew from Dun Morogh’s frozen heights to the warmer valley.

Mountaineer Barleybrew thinks Rejold’s new Shimmer Stout is too good to keep in Dun Morogh. From the eastern border post, he watches over the mountain passes and the kin guarding neighboring lands. The Mountaineers’ patrols can be cold and grueling, and a stout heart calls for stout drink. Barleybrew wants an honest opinion from a fellow patrolman, so he sends a cask east with travelers bound for Loch Modan.

For young dwarven and gnomish adventurers, the road to Loch Modan is a rite of passage after their early days in Dun Morogh’s snowbound crags. You pass southeast through the South Gate Outpost and follow long tunnels cut through the mountain bedrock. Beyond them lies Loch Modan’s warmer, wooded basin. Mountaineer Kadrell patrols the road through Thelsamar. He gladly pauses to tap the cask and finds that Barleybrew’s new recipe has an astonishing kick.
Mountaineer Kadrell is a dwarven defender in Loch Modan. He patrols the central road through Thelsamar.

As an Alliance traveler, the road leads from Dun Morogh’s snowy reaches into Loch Modan’s broader frontier.
As a dwarf, carrying mountain ale across territorial lines connects Brewnall Village’s brewers with the patrols guarding Khaz Modan.

Barleybrew is on active watch at the South Gate Outpost, tasked with guarding Dun Morogh's eastern borders and monitoring travelers. As a Mountaineer on duty, he cannot abandon his post simply to share a drink, leaving him dependent on passing adventurers traveling southeast toward Loch Modan to carry the cask to Kadrell.

In Dun Morogh, Rejold's New Brew brings you back to Brewnall Village. After you gathered Shimmerweed, Rejold Barleybrew has perfected a new recipe and wants you, a trusted friend, to sample it.

Tharek Blackstone and Pilot Bellowfiz, your contacts in Dun Morogh, send you back to Brewnall Village. Rejold Barleybrew has finished fermenting his experimental batches and wants to share them with the traveler who made them possible: you, after securing Shimmerweed from the bitter slopes.

Brewnall Village is known for its ale craft, and Rejold Barleybrew’s newest batch is no ordinary draught. He infused his mash with local herbs to make Shimmer Stout. Before shipping barrels to neighboring outposts and thirsty patrons in Loch Modan, Rejold insists that you, the adventurer who risked life and limb for the herbs, have the honor of the first sip.
